title: Rauno Freiberg reviews 40 portfolios
lede: On 2026-10-19 Rauno Freiberg asked people to send their portfolios and answered 40 of them in a thread. Each review is pinned here onto the page it is about: what he said, what the page shows, how he seems to have got there, and where the idea belongs in plumber. His words are retold in ours; each review links to his reply.

points.says: It looks very much like read.cv, and he likes that.
points.shows: A single narrow column of small text on an empty page, a name, one line about the job, then short labelled lists. That is the layout the profile site read.cv made familiar.
points.how: He placed the site in a family he already knows before judging anything in it. Everything after this is judged against what that family promises: calm, text first, nothing in the way.
points.engine: Shape: which known kind of page this is. Plumber has no idea of kinds of page. A model that has seen many sites could name the kind, and the kind then says what to expect.
points.engine_case_why_not: The site turns our browser away.

points.says: The first thing he did was make the text bigger, and he has perfect eyesight and a large display. Body text at 15 or 16 would work better; 15 is his current favourite.
points.shows: In his recording the body text measures about 13px with a 20px line, in a column about 546 pixels wide on a window 1,426 wide. On the page today the same text is 16px and the small text 14px.
points.how: He did not measure anything. He noticed what his own hand did: he reached for zoom before reading a word. If a reader with good eyes on a good screen has to do that, the size is wrong, whatever the number is. The number came afterwards, from what he has settled on in his own work.
points.engine: Craft: body text that is too small. A plain reading of the size of running text, which plumber can already take. The threshold is his (15 to 16) and would need its own source. The larger lesson is the test he used: what does a reader do first.
points.today: Fixed: body text went from about 13px to 16px.
points.unseen: The 13px is an estimate from frames of his recording, not a reading of the page.
points.engine_case_why_not: No longer on the page.

points.says: Pressing a post on the blog list does not open it. The page only plays its little animation. He suspects something is taking the clicks.
points.shows: In the recording he presses the post title and a burst of small characters appears where he pressed, the site’s pointer effect. The page stays where it is.
points.how: A press on a title in a list has one expected result: the thing opens. He pressed, saw decoration answer in place of the page, and named the likely cause straight away, an invisible layer on top of the link.
points.engine: Behaviour: a control that something else covers. Plumber has a check for a control with another element on top of it. Whether it catches this case is not tested. The effect layer here is the kind of thing that check should look for.
points.today: Not checked by pressing. The post title is a link in today’s page.

has.name: Something sits on top of this
has.note: Not tried on this page.

points.engine_case_why_not: The site turns our browser away.

points.says: A few links in the command menu are broken.
points.shows: The menu lists pages, settings and actions, some marked with an arrow for links that leave the site. The recording does not show which ones failed.
points.how: He opened the menu and tried the entries one after another. A menu is a list of promises; he checked each one.
points.engine: Behaviour: a link that leads nowhere. It needs every link followed and the answer read, which the page check does not do today.
points.today: Not checked.
points.unseen: Which links failed. His recording does not show it and we did not press them.
points.engine_case_why_not: The site turns our browser away.

points.says: Going to Crafts shows an ugly flash of the page without its styles.
points.shows: Crafts is a separate site with its own typefaces and layout. The flash of an unstyled page while it loads is his report.
points.how: He watched the moment between two pages. A page is judged while it arrives too, and here the first thing it showed was its unfinished state.
points.engine: Behaviour over time: what a page looks like in its first moments. Plumber reads a page once it has settled. It would need to look at the first frames of a page arriving and compare them with the settled page.
points.today: Not checked.
points.unseen: The flash. We did not watch the page arrive.
points.engine_case_why_not: The site turns our browser away.

points.says: Every surface feels like a different portfolio: home, the command menu, Crafts and the blog.
points.shows: Home and the blog are small grey text in one column. The command menu is a warm tinted panel with rounded rows and a peach highlight. Crafts has a large serif heading and a grid of bordered cards with colourful pictures. Nothing is shared between them: not the typeface, not the colours, not the density.
points.how: He moved through the site and kept a picture of each place in mind. Each one is good alone. Side by side they do not look made by the same hand, and a portfolio is exactly the place where that is being judged.
points.engine: Shape, across pages: one visual language through a whole site. Plumber judges one page at a time. It would need a short description of each page’s look (typefaces, colours, corner sizes, density) and a way to say when one page shares too little with the others. The same judgement returns in his review of his own site and in the shadcn favicon.
points.today: Not checked. The owner said he was in the middle of moving the site to a different stack.
points.engine_case_why_not: The site turns our browser away.

reviews.note: The pins are on frames from Rauno’s own recording, so they show the site as he saw it. The site sits behind a check that turned our server’s browser away, so today’s picture comes from the browser pane.

reviews.who: Rauno Freiberg, on his own site (posted by @joshpuckett)

shots.label: Home as the web archive saved it on 2026-10-17, two days before the thread
Craft, same archive day
Projects, same archive day
Field Notes, same archive day

points.says: The reveal animation, where content is uncovered by a moving cut-out, belongs to 2020.
points.shows: The home page holds large shapes, such as a yellow circle. How they arrive is his report: content uncovered by a moving cut-out.
points.how: He knows when an effect was in fashion, and an effect that everyone used in one year dates the work to that year. This is knowledge of the field, not something on the page.
points.engine: Taste, tied to time. Plumber cannot know what is dated. The nearest thing it has is its family of checks for marks of a period or of a generated page. A model that has seen many sites by year could say “this effect peaked in 2020”. To be looked at live.
points.unseen: The animation. We did not watch the page arrive, so which effect he means is our guess.

points.says: Why be clever. Why not scroll down like everything else.
points.shows: The home page is a row of large sheets laid side by side, 6,648 pixels wide. You move through it sideways. The next sheet is cut off at the right edge of the screen.
points.how: Scrolling down is the one gesture every visitor already knows. A page that asks for another gesture spends the visitor’s attention on how to move, and gets nothing back for it.
points.engine: Behaviour: a page whose main direction is sideways. Plumber can read it directly: the page is far wider than the window and no taller. The same idea is in review 15, where a list scrolls sideways and a mouse wheel cannot move it.

has.name: Page scrolls sideways
has.note: Plumber reads a page that scrolls sideways as an accident. Here it is the design.

has.name: More to the side, and no sign of it

points.says: Can he do something other than a white sheet on a grey canvas.
points.shows: Every page of the site is the same recipe: white rounded sheets on a light grey ground (the ground is rgb 237, 237, 237).
points.how: He recognises a recipe that has become a default, his own included. Once a look is everywhere it stops saying anything about the person who chose it.
points.engine: Shape, as a cliché. This is the same family as plumber’s checks for marks of a generated screen: a look that is common enough to be a tell. It needs knowledge of what is common, which comes from many sites, not from this one.

points.says: Writing about yourself in the third person is a pose.
points.shows: The headline reads “Rauno Freiberg is an Estonian interaction designer working with Vercel and Devouring Details”, set at 85px.
points.how: On a personal site the reader knows who is speaking. Third person puts on a voice from a press release, and he hears it as trying to look important.
points.engine: Content and voice. Only a model that reads the words can judge it. Not a check on what is drawn.
points.engine_case_why_not: Advice about the work, not about the page.

points.says: The navigation is too obscure, and it does not cover pages deeper in the site.
points.shows: The whole navigation is a strip of three small empty rectangles with thin strokes between them, 194 pixels wide at the top centre. The current page’s rectangle is filled yellow. There are no words. Field Notes has no rectangle at all, so on that page nothing is marked.
points.how: He asked two things of it. Can a stranger tell what each mark is and where they are now? No: three identical boxes. Does every page have a place in it? No: some addresses fall outside it. A navigation that needs to be learned and still has gaps is failing at its only job.
points.engine: Shape: controls that look identical and carry no words, and a current page with no marked item. Plumber already flags a control with no name a screen reader can say. The second half, a page that is in no menu, needs the menu’s links compared with the page’s own address.

has.name: No name for screen readers
has.note: The first half: controls with no words.

has.name: Navigation does not mark this page
has.note: For a screen reader, not for the eye.

points.says: You cannot tell which links open a new tab and which stay on the site.
points.shows: The sheets on the home page are all links and all look alike. Devouring Details and History of Software Design leave the site; Craft, Projects and Field Notes stay. On Craft the button says “View Production” for some and “Read Essay” for others, with no mark of where each goes.
points.how: Leaving a site is a different act from moving inside it, and a visitor wants to know which one they are about to do. Here the two kinds of link look the same, so every click is a small gamble. He says the same to two other people in the thread.
points.engine: Shape: alike, but not the same role. Plumber can read where each link goes and whether it opens a new tab, then find groups of links that look the same and mix the two kinds. Review 36 gives the limit: a link whose own words name another place (GitHub, X, mail) needs no mark.

points.says: His essays, the deep work, are buried next to flashy clips.
points.shows: Craft is three columns of cards, about 9,600 pixels tall. An essay card (“Novelty”, with a “Read Essay” button) is one card among short looping clips, the same size and style as the rest.
points.how: He ranked his own content by worth and then looked at what the page ranks first. The page gives the essays the same weight as eye-catching clips, and moving pictures win the eye. So what he values most is what a visitor is least likely to find.
points.engine: Shape: the loudest thing should be what matters most. Plumber can measure what is loud (motion, size, colour). What matters most here is the author’s own judgement, which no reading of the page gives. A model can guess (an essay outranks a clip), with low certainty.

points.says: On Craft it is easy to miss which entries can be clicked.
points.shows: Some cards are links and some are only clips. The single cue is a pale grey bar under the card with two words on it. A card without the bar looks the same in every other way.
points.how: The reverse of what he told shadcn. There, things looked clickable and were not. Here things are clickable and barely look it. He scanned the grid and could not sort the cards by eye.
points.engine: Shape: the same role, but not alike enough to be seen as a group. Plumber can list which cards are links and compare how they look with the ones that are not. If the difference is one faint bar, the two groups are too alike.

points.says: Each page is its own world from its own period. Only the navigation ties them together.
points.shows: Home is huge type on white sheets. Craft is a dense grid of clips. Projects is nine short lines in the middle of an empty page. Field Notes is full-screen red lettering. They share the strip at the top and little else.
points.how: The same judgement he gave the first site in the thread, turned on himself: he walked through the pages and they do not look made at one time by one hand.
points.engine: Shape, across pages. The same new reading as point 1.6: a short description of each page’s look and a way to compare them.

points.says: The navigation throws some pages off balance.
points.shows: On Projects the strip sits alone at the top centre, far above a short list that starts a third of the way down. On Craft it floats above three full columns.
points.how: He looked at each page as a composition and asked whether the strip belongs to it. A fixed element that suits one page’s weight can sit awkwardly on another whose content is lighter or placed elsewhere.
points.engine: Shape: balance. Plumber could compare where the visual weight of the content sits with where the fixed element sits, page by page. The research we read warns that scores of whole-page balance match human judgement only modestly, so this would be a weak signal.

points.says: A joke: four more reasons the navigation is bad, with none given.
points.shows: Nothing to show. It is his third remark about the navigation in twelve lines.
points.how: The repetition is the information: of everything on his site, the navigation is what he regrets most.
points.engine: Nothing to build. It adds weight to points 3.5 and 3.10.
points.unseen: Nothing to see: it is a joke with no content.
points.engine_case_why_not: Advice about the work, not about the page.

points.says: Projects and Craft overlap, and one is far heavier than the other.
points.shows: Projects is nine links. Craft is about 9,600 pixels of cards. History of Software Design and Devouring Details appear on both.
points.how: He asked what each page is for. Two pages that answer the same question, one long and one almost empty, mean the site’s structure was never decided.
points.engine: Content and structure, across pages. Plumber could notice the same destinations listed on two pages and a large difference in how much each page holds. Whether that is a fault needs judgement.
points.engine_case_why_not: Advice about the work, not about the page.

reviews.note: He wrote this about his own site after a friend posted it as a joke, so each line is a rule he holds, stated without softening. The archive copy is from two days before.

shots.label: First screen on 2026-11-26 at 2560 pixels wide, the width of the display he reviewed on

points.says: The row of project tiles is cut off carelessly. It ends neither on the page’s vertical line nor on the edge of the white area.
points.shows: The page is a white area between two vertical lines, with a narrower column of content inside it. The tiles slide sideways in a row that is wider than the screen, so the row has to be cut somewhere. Today, at his width, it is cut exactly on the two vertical lines. The owner answered that it looked fine on his own screen and that he had not thought about other screens, so what Rauno saw was a cut that fell between the lines on a wide display.
points.how: A place where things are cut off is an edge, and the eye reads every edge as a decision. This page already draws its edges: two vertical lines and a content column. An edge that lands on neither one is a new line with no reason behind it, and that reads as sloppy. He saw it because his display is much wider than the one the page was built on.
points.engine: Shape: every edge should sit on a line the layout already has. Plumber can list the places where content is cut (boxes that hide what overflows them) and check that each cut lands on a container edge or a shared line. It has to look at several widths, a very wide one included, because the fault only exists there. The wide look is the new part.
points.today: No fault at 2,560 wide today: the row ends on the two vertical lines. Whether that is a fix is not known. The web archive only has this site from April, six months before the review.
points.unseen: The cut he saw. Today the row ends on the two lines at 2,560 wide. Whether the owner changed it or his window was another width is not known.

points.says: The four section links in the hero are not much use. Choosing one scrolls you down the page, and after that you cannot get back to them.
points.shows: Under the introduction sit four links with counts: product releases, design systems, iOS and macOS apps, AI work and labs. Three of them jump to a section further down this long page (about 6,600 pixels). They live only in the hero. The bar at the top holds different links, to other pages.
points.how: He used it. He picked one section, landed there, wanted the next one, and found the control had left the screen. A menu that takes you away from itself works once. Navigation has to stay within reach of every place it sends you.
points.engine: Behaviour: a set of links that scroll the same page should still be reachable after one is followed. Plumber already tries gestures on a page. This one would follow a same-page link, then ask whether the group it belonged to is still on screen or pinned. Needs a new gesture, no new idea.
points.today: Unchanged on 2026-11-26.

points.says: Make the logo smaller and the text bigger. His eyes skip the big wordmark, however long it took to make, because eyes go to words that say something.
points.shows: The largest thing on the first screen after the photo is the name drawn as a logo, a picture about 480 pixels wide. The two lines that say who he is are 17px, in black at half strength. Body text elsewhere on the site is set at 12px.
points.how: A logo is recognised in a glance and then there is nothing left in it to read. A sentence keeps the eye because it carries news. So size should go to the thing that carries information, not to the thing that took effort. He noticed his own eye passing over the wordmark and going looking for text.
points.engine: Shape: the loudest thing on a screen should be the thing that says the most. Plumber can already rank what is biggest and darkest on the first screen. Knowing that a sentence about the person says more than their name drawn as a picture needs a judgement about meaning, which is the job for a model.
points.today: Unchanged on 2026-11-26.

reviews.note: What he saw in October could not be recovered for this site; the pins are on today’s page at his display width.

points.says: Hovering the two photos in the hero feels abrupt. The one behind jumps in front at once, and that is not satisfying.
points.shows: Two tilted photos overlap in the hero, a smaller one behind and a larger one in front. Under the pointer the one behind is drawn on top by the very next frame, about 20 thousandths of a second later. Only then does it start to grow, by about 5 percent, and that takes more than a second to settle. So the order changes before anything has moved, and the movement that follows explains nothing.
points.how: Something coming forward is a physical event: it lifts, travels and settles. A photo that is suddenly on top has skipped the event. He felt the missing movement before he looked for the cause, then named the cause exactly, the stacking order changing with nothing in between.
points.engine: Behaviour: a change that cannot be eased, used where a movement is expected. Plumber already tries hovering things and reads what changes. It could say when a hover changes which element is on top while nothing moves or fades to carry it.
points.today: Unchanged. Tried and timed on the live page on 2026-11-26.

scene.try: Move the pointer onto the photo behind, then away. Watch the moment it comes to the front.

case.state: After the opening screen, with the pointer moved onto the photo behind.
case.signal: Under the pointer one thing comes to the front of another it overlaps. The order changes in the first frame, and its own movement takes about a second.
case.measured: Stacking order 1 to 3 at 23 ms. Scale 1.00 to 1.05, still settling at 1,055 ms. Read every frame on the live page, 2026-11-26.

expect.say: Comes to the front at once, then moves. (Our wording, not his.)

case.insight: A change of order between overlapping things has no in-between. Paired with a movement, it has to happen where the movement has carried the two clear of each other, or the eye sees a cut.

plumber.why: The page check read no elements on this site, on the home page and on a project page. It judges only elements tied to the app’s own source, and a public site has none.

points.says: Two similar photos of yourself may not help. Dig for an idea: the favicon is already a drawn avatar of him, so something clever could be done with showing himself as photo and as avatar.
points.shows: Both pictures are casual photos of the same person, one standing in a field and one close up in a street. The site’s tab icon is a drawn portrait of him.
points.how: Each thing on a page should add something the others do not. The second photo repeats the first. He then looked around the site for material already there, found the drawn portrait in the tab, and proposed joining the two into one idea. It is the same habit as with shadcn’s favicon: he reads the tab icon as part of the design.
points.engine: Content and concept. A model could notice two pictures of the same subject side by side; whether that is redundant is taste. Nothing to check in what is drawn.
points.today: Unchanged on 2026-11-26.
points.engine_case_why_not: Advice about the work, not about the page.

points.says: The case studies are behind a password. He understands why, but a visitor without the password is left with a few screen recordings. Put something on the table for everyone else.
points.shows: All four projects carry a lock beside their title. Each card plays a recording of the product, and hovering it says the case study is password protected. Pressing a card opens a page that holds one password box and two buttons.
points.how: He arrived as the visitor the page was not built for: someone without the key. From there the site has almost nothing to say. A page should be judged from its worst-equipped visitor too, the way an app is judged by its empty state.
points.engine: Content and flow: a list where the main items lead to a locked door. Plumber could follow the links and see that they end at a password form. Deciding that this leaves too little for the public is a judgement about content.
points.today: Unchanged on 2026-11-26: four projects, four locks.

scene.try: Press any of the four projects. Each one opens on a password box and nothing else.

points.engine_case_why_not: Advice about the work, not about the page.

reviews.note: Redone on 2026-11-26 by using the live site as he did. The site opens with a screen of the name that lasts about five seconds; this view skips it. The page scrolls inside a box of its own, which is why the earlier boxes did not follow it.

shots.label: A project opened, a frame from his own screen recording on 2026-10-19
Home in the same recording

points.says: A viewer for stepping through work is basic equipment. If he cannot see at once how to move through it, he closes the tab.
points.shows: Pressing a tile opens the piece alone on a dark screen, with a strip of small thumbnails along the bottom. There are no arrows on the screen. A round arrow, pointing left or right, appears only at the pointer, depending on which side of the screen the pointer is. In his recording the pointer wanders before he finds it.
points.how: Some parts of a site are places to be inventive and some are plumbing. Stepping to the next picture is plumbing: everyone has done it a thousand times and expects it to work without thought. He gave it a second, did not see how, and stated the cost plainly: the visitor leaves. The owner’s answer calls it an accessibility fix, which is the same fault seen from the keyboard.
points.engine: Behaviour: a control that cannot be seen until you are already on it. Plumber already flags controls with no name. Here it would ask, for anything that opens a set of items one at a time, whether a next and a previous control are visible and can be reached by keyboard.
points.today: Not checked. The owner said he was fixing it.

points.says: The transitions feel slow.
points.shows: In the recording, opening a piece and moving between pieces each take long enough to watch. He gives no number.
points.how: Movement between items of the same kind is travel, and travel should be nearly free. When he has to wait for an animation before he can look at the next thing, the animation is in the way. He says the same to two other people, each time about pages meant to feel quick.
points.engine: Behaviour: how long a movement takes. Plumber has checks on motion and can read how long a transition runs. It has no principle yet for how long is too long when moving between items; his remark is a lead, and the number needs its own source.
points.today: Not checked.
points.unseen: How long. We watched his recording and did not time it.

has.name: Leaves as slowly as it came
Shortcut opens slowly
has.note: One case of the same reason: do not make people wait on motion.

reviews.note: His recording is the evidence here. The web archive only has this site from May.

shots.label: The whole home page on 2026-11-26

points.says: The dithered picture style is out of fashion.
points.shows: The hero is a photo of a bridge turned into coarse black dots, in a rounded card 380 pixels wide.
points.how: Knowledge of the field, as with the dated animation on his own site. A treatment that was everywhere for a season now marks a page as following that season.
points.engine: Taste, tied to time. The same family as plumber’s checks for marks of a period. Recognising a dithered picture needs a model that looks at the image.
points.today: The picture is still there. The owner answered that he meant to build on it.

points.says: The page would look clearly better with the hero picture removed.
points.shows: The picture fills most of the first screen. His name starts 655 pixels down, and the first line about what he does is below that. Everything under the picture is plain text in one column 512 pixels wide.
points.how: He ran the page without the element in his head and compared. The picture says nothing about the person, and it pushes everything that does off the first screen. When taking something away makes the page better, the thing was costing more than it gave.
points.engine: Shape: the largest thing on the first screen should carry meaning. Plumber can measure how much of the first screen a picture takes and how far down the first words are. That the picture says nothing about him is a judgement of content, for a model.
points.today: Unchanged.

points.says: He likes the small game but it is too close to the dinosaur game in Chrome. Push it further, make it his own, and let it run the full width of the window. That would also break the rigid look of a résumé. It could even replace the hero picture.
points.shows: The game is a canvas 512 by 183 pixels, the same width as every other block on the page, near the bottom under the heading “Journey”.
points.how: Two thoughts. A borrowed idea has to be changed enough to become yours. And a page where every block has the same width has no accent: the one piece with character should be the one allowed to break the column. He is moving emphasis to where the personality is.
points.engine: Shape: rhythm. Plumber can see that every block shares one width, so nothing is set apart. It cannot say which block deserves to break out; that is a design proposal. This belongs with the layout generator more than with a check.
points.today: The game is still the width of the column.

points.says: The rows under Work cannot be clicked across their whole width, only on the name.
points.shows: Each row is a year, a name and a short description on one line. Today the whole row, 512 by 45 pixels, is one link.
points.how: He clicked where the row is, not where the word is. A row reads as one object, so the whole object should answer. He found the gap by missing.
points.engine: Craft: the part that answers a click is smaller than the thing that looks clickable. Plumber has a check for strips between rows that do nothing. This is its neighbour: compare each link’s own box with the box of the row it sits in.
points.today: Fixed: the whole row is the link.
points.unseen: The page he saw could not be recovered. Only today’s page was read.
points.engine_case_why_not: No longer on the page.

reviews.note: The web archive has no copy of this site, so the pins are on today’s page.

shots.label: The picture Rauno attached: a project visual he found deeper in the site
Home on 2026-11-26, marked “Updated October 2026”

points.says: The page shows a scrollbar even when there is nothing to scroll. Set the system to always show scrollbars and you will catch it.
points.shows: His report, with the way to see it. On a Mac scrollbars hide until you scroll, so a page that forces one looks fine to its author.
points.how: He keeps his system set to show scrollbars all the time, on purpose, because it shows faults the default hides. He is not reporting a bug so much as handing over the test that finds a whole family of them.
points.engine: Craft, and a condition to look under. Plumber has a check for scrolling that is switched on all the time when it should appear only when needed. His advice adds the condition: read the page with classic, always-visible scrollbars, the way plumber already re-reads it at larger text.
points.today: Not checked.
points.unseen: The empty scrollbar track. We did not read the page with scrollbars always shown.

points.says: There is no point in thumbnails this small. Nothing in them can be made out.
points.shows: What he saw could not be recovered: the archive copy is broken. Today each project shows pictures 546 pixels wide in a row that runs off the right edge.
points.how: A picture has a job, to show the thing. Below some size it stops doing the job and becomes a grey patch that still takes room and attention. The same judgement as the sponsor faces on shadcn’s page.
points.engine: Craft: a picture drawn too small for what it holds. Plumber can compare the size a picture is drawn at with the size it was made at. Whether its content survives the shrink needs a look at the picture itself.
points.today: Fixed: the pictures are large.
points.unseen: The page he saw could not be recovered. Only today’s page was read.
points.engine_case_why_not: No longer on the page.

points.says: He has beautiful pictures of his projects, like the one attached. Why are they not on the front page?
points.shows: The picture he attached is a careful render of an old computer running a terminal, from one project’s own page. The front page at the time led with text and the tiny thumbnails.
points.how: He went one level down, found the best thing on the site, and asked why a visitor has to dig for it. Most visitors judge from the first page and never go deeper. He says the same to four other people in this thread: lead with your strongest material.

points.says: The slow page transitions clash with the look of the site, which is a terminal-like operating system obsessed with speed.
points.shows: The home page is drawn as a desktop: a bar across the top with a clock, folders and files as icons, monospaced labels. By his report opening something plays a slow transition.
points.how: The same judgement he gave the site before this one. He read what the look promises, a machine that answers at once, and the first click took its time. A computer desktop that eases gently between windows is acting against its own costume.
points.engine: Behaviour against shape: the motion should agree with what the look says. Plumber can time the transition. Reading the page as “an operating system” is the judgement about kinds of page from point 1.1.
points.today: Not checked. For the live harness.

points.says: Writing and projects do not look different at a glance, so they blend together.
points.shows: Two panels sit side by side. Both are white boxes with the same hairline border, the same small capital heading, the same monospaced titles with a grey line under each, and a “View all” link at the bottom. Only the words tell them apart.
points.how: Two things that are different in kind are drawn as the same thing twice. Likeness says “same”, so the eye files them together and has to read to separate them. He wants the difference in kind to be visible before reading. It is the mirror of the headings on shadcn’s page.
points.engine: Shape: different roles, but alike. Plumber can compare two neighbouring groups and find that every drawn property matches while their contents differ in kind (dated articles on one side, tools with year ranges on the other). The contents’ kinds can be read partly from structure.
points.today: The two panels still share one style.

points.says: Some elements, the badges for example, seem to come from another world. It feels only half committed to the operating-system idea.
points.shows: Under each project are grey rounded pills holding years. The rest of the page borrows from a desktop: folders, file names with extensions, a path in the top bar. A rounded pill is from web apps, not from a desktop.
points.how: Once a page takes on a metaphor, every element is checked against it, and the ones that do not belong stand out more than they would on a plain page. Half a metaphor is weaker than none, because it shows where the idea ran out.
points.engine: Shape: one visual language, and the odd element out. Plumber could notice that one kind of element has a look (rounded, filled, grey) that nothing else on the page shares. Knowing that it breaks “an operating system” needs the judgement about kinds of page again.
points.today: The pills are still there.

shots.label: The picture Rauno attached: he drew a box round each block of content and wrote its size and proportions on it
His second picture: a testimonial with its five stars

points.says: The content makes unsatisfying shapes that look cluttered on the page. If it were more cluttered it would get interesting. As it is, it sits in an awkward middle.
points.shows: His picture is the argument. He drew a box round the three blocks on the first screen and labelled them: the introduction, 554 by 280, about 2 to 1; the photo, 344 by 412, about 6 to 7; the poem, 251 by 310, about 4 to 5. Three different proportions. The three boxes share no edge: each starts at a different left, and the photo and the poem start 45 pixels apart in height.
points.how: He stopped reading and looked at the outlines. Each block is a rectangle with a proportion and a position, and the page is the arrangement of those rectangles. Here the proportions are unrelated and the edges nearly line up but do not. Then he gives the rule in one line: order reads as intended, real disorder reads as intended, and the space between reads as an accident.
points.engine: Shape, and the plainest confirmation in the thread of the idea this work started from. Take the bounding box of each block. Compare their proportions and their edges. Exact agreement is fine, a large difference is a choice, and a near miss is the fault. Plumber has the boxes already. Our research note gives the count for regularity; his picture shows an expert doing the same thing by hand.
points.today: Not checked.

has.name: Lines start on different edges
has.note: Inside cards in a row only.

points.says: There is perhaps 45 percent too much yellow in the text. When many parts are highlighted, the highlight no longer picks anything out. Yellow is also a very strong colour and hard to keep under control.
points.shows: In the introduction most of the words are yellow and a few are white. Counting letters on the archived page: 226 yellow against 135 white, so 63 percent of the text is in the highlight colour.
points.how: A highlight works by being the exception. Once it covers most of the text, the plain words become the exception, and here the white ones are what stands out. This is the second rule of loudness from the research we read: a thing stands out only while its neighbours are alike and it is not. He adds a note on the colour itself: the stronger the colour, the less of it a page can carry.
points.engine: Shape: emphasis used so much that it stops being emphasis. Plumber can measure what share of a block of text is in its accent colour and say when the accent has become the majority. A plain reading of colours it already takes.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: The “Making” section has great hand-drawn art for each item. Why is it so tiny? Make it big.
points.shows: Each item under Making has a drawing beside its name, shown 32 pixels wide. The files behind them are 947, 1,148 and 303 pixels wide.
points.how: He found the best material on the page being used as a bullet point. Size should follow worth. The drawings are the most personal thing she has made, so they should be the largest thing in that section, not the smallest.
points.engine: Content, with a signal plumber already reads: a picture drawn at a small fraction of the size it was made at. Plumber’s check says the file is too big for its place and should be smaller. He says the place is too small for the drawing. One reading, two opposite fixes; which one holds depends on what the picture is.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: When he hovers the picture it changes its position and its border, so he expects it to do something.

points.engine: Behaviour, and “looks like a control, is not one”. Plumber already tries hovering things and reads what changes. It could say when an element answers a hover clearly and is neither a link nor a control.

points.says: He read the testimonial as zero stars, because the stars are not filled in.
points.shows: Each testimonial is headed by five star outlines. They are meant as five out of five.
points.how: Rating stars are a small language everybody knows: filled means earned, outline means empty. Five outlines say nought out of five, the opposite of what was meant. He read the picture before the words, as visitors do.
points.engine: Shape: a familiar symbol used against its meaning. Plumber could recognise a row of five star characters and see that they are the outline kind. A small specific check, and a good example of a convention that has to be known to be checked.

points.says: The home page forgets which parts he has already unlocked and read when he comes back from another page.
points.shows: The introduction is a long blurred text. A few phrases are clear and end in a pill, such as PEDRO, RAYCAST and BARCELONA. Pressing a pill clears more of the text, and a counter at the top right keeps score out of 15. By his report, leaving the page and returning sets it back to nought.
points.how: He did some work on the page, left, came back, and the work was gone. Anything a visitor has done is theirs. A page that throws it away tells them not to bother a second time.
points.engine: Behaviour: state lost on the way back. Plumber could change something on a page, follow a link, come back and compare. A new gesture built from ones it has.
points.today: Not checked.
points.unseen: The reset. We did not leave the page and come back.

points.says: He can move the keyboard focus onto the pills inside the blurred text, but they cannot be read when focused.
points.shows: Pills further along sit inside text that is still blurred. By his report the Tab key reaches them, and the focus lands on something that cannot be read.
points.how: He walks through every page with the keyboard as well as the mouse. Focus must always land on something a person can see and understand. Here the keyboard can go where the eye cannot follow.
points.engine: Craft, and close to a check plumber has: something that can be tabbed to while hidden from screen readers. This is its visual twin: something that can be tabbed to while blurred. Plumber can read the blur on whatever takes focus.
points.today: Not checked.
points.unseen: The focus on blurred text. We did not walk the Tab key through it.

points.says: On a phone, in Safari, the bars at the top and bottom do not match the body of the page.
points.shows: In his phone picture the page is near black and so is the area behind the status bar. The area behind the browser’s bottom bar is white.
points.how: On a phone the browser paints its own strips above and below the page, in a colour the page can set. He treats those strips as part of the design. A dark page between a dark strip and a white one looks unfinished. The same habit as with favicons and share pictures: the page includes its frame.
points.engine: Craft, on a surface around the page. Plumber has a neighbour: a dark page whose browser parts stay light, because the page never says it is dark. The bars of a phone browser take their colour from two other things, the declared theme colour and the colour behind the page. Reading those would be new.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: He can pull the page past its end, the elastic way phones allow, and that reveals the video underneath. It looks like a bug.
points.shows: In his picture the dark page has been pulled up and a grey video of a person shows below it, where nothing should be.
points.how: He pulls every page past its edges, because phones let anyone do it. What is behind the page at that moment was never meant to be seen, and here it is a layer the design relies on. A hidden mechanism showing through reads as breakage.
points.engine: Behaviour, under another condition: the page pulled past its end. Plumber could find layers fixed behind the page and ask what would show if the page were pulled away from the edge of the window. A new condition, in the same family as scrollbars always visible.
points.today: Not checked.

points.how: The page has one strong idea, words in the text that open things, and a menu that does the same job the ordinary way beside it. He sees the two could be one. As with the half-finished desktop in review 38, an idea is strongest when everything on the page uses it.
points.engine: Content and concept. Plumber could notice that words in the body match the names of pages in the menu and are not links to them. Whether they should be is a design idea.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: On a phone, bring the menu back at the end of a long article, to save him from a dead end. With a design this restrained, the list of articles could even be shown at the end of each article, so that he does not have to go back or scroll all the way up.
points.shows: His phone picture shows the last line of an article, a thank-you to a proof-reader, and then empty page down to the browser’s bar. The menu is at the top of the page, many screens above.
points.how: He read to the end, which is the best thing a visitor can do, and the page rewarded him with nothing. The end of an article is where a reader decides whether to read another. He offers the smallest fix, the menu again, and then a better one that suits this plain design.
points.engine: Behaviour: a long page with no way onward at its end. Plumber can measure how far the nearest link to another page is from the bottom of a long page, at phone width. The same family as the dead end in review 41.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: There is an odd highlight between characters in the code blocks.
points.shows: In his enlarged picture each highlighted word has a pale yellow background. Where two highlighted words meet, their backgrounds overlap by a few pixels and the overlap is a darker yellow strip. He underlined four of them in red.
points.how: He zoomed in. The backgrounds are see-through, so two of them stacked make a stronger colour, and the join shows. At normal size it reads as a faint flicker in the code that is hard to place. He places it.
points.engine: Craft: see-through backgrounds on neighbours that overlap. Plumber can find neighbouring pieces of text that each have a partly transparent background and whose boxes overlap. An exact check with what it already reads.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: The code blocks could use the CSS properties that style a scrollbar.
points.shows: Under a code block sits the browser’s default scrollbar, a thick grey bar, on a page where everything else is thin and quiet.
points.how: One part of the page was left as the browser draws it, and it is the heaviest thing in view. A default beside careful work reads as a spot that was missed. Layr’s reference lists this exact signal under polish.
points.engine: Craft: a browser default left in a styled page. Plumber can see a box that scrolls sideways and has no scrollbar styling while the rest of the page is styled. Best read with scrollbars always shown.
points.today: Not checked.

points.says: When he has scrolled all the way down an article and goes to the index, the motion is jarring. Such moments could be made instant as a special case.
points.shows: In his recording he presses “about” in the side menu from deep in an article. For a few frames the content area is empty while the page changes and the scroll position jumps to the top, then the new page appears.
points.how: A transition designed for a page at rest is being played from a page scrolled far down, so the animation and the jump back to the top fight each other. He does not ask for a better animation. He asks for none in this case: when two movements would collide, drop one.
points.engine: Behaviour: a transition tried from a state its designer did not picture. Plumber could follow a link once from the top of a page and once from the bottom and compare how much moves in between. The lesson for ranking: an instant change is a correct answer.
points.today: Not checked. For the live harness.

points.says: The bullets of his lists do not follow the vertical line that the typography has set.
points.shows: His report: in a list, the bullets do not sit on the left edge that the paragraphs share.
points.how: A column of text draws a line down the page with its left edge, and the eye runs along it. Anything that starts a little to one side of that line reads as slightly loose. He names the line, the key line, which is how people who set type talk about it.
points.engine: Shape: edges that should share a line. Plumber has this judgement inside one group: rows of a menu or a list whose words start a few pixels off the edge the others keep. His case is across groups, a list against the paragraphs around it, which plumber does not compare.
